comparator.design: The reference path is deliberately a different algorithm from production: it copies the root bounds and replays every recorded branching step chronologically, while NodeBounds::materialize walks the delta chain from tail to root and applies it root-first. NodeView comparison additionally replays the scoped cut list against the concatenation of recorded local cuts and runs production through the budgeted NodeView::materialize on an internal budget sized exactly for the comparison.
comparator.caps: ReferenceCaps {max_variables, max_steps, max_bytes} covers vectors, steps and total cut ids; preflight refuses before any allocation, and refusal/invalid results report reference_bytes=0. Statuses: ok, mismatch (facet + first_mismatch_index: lower_bounds/upper_bounds/cut_scope/production), refused, invalid, allocation_failed.
comparator.coverage: 200 randomized chains (1-12 variables, depth 1-10, repeated writes to the same variable so chain order is observable), 400-op randomized push/pop against full reconstruction of the retained prefix, sibling bounds+cut isolation including parent immutability after branching, refusal on each cap plus cut-total overflow, mismatch detection with exact facet/index (extra delta, wrong value, upper surface, cut position), invalid inputs (dimension mismatch, out-of-range step). node_view_reference_identity_test solves the node LP from production-materialized and reference-replayed vectors and requires bit-identical status/objective/primal, then verifies the full-solve incumbent against the original model with verify_primal.

structural_accounting.method: Capacity-based byte accounting per storage class (frontier_storage_bytes.hpp): root = matrix arrays + objective + variable bounds/types; worker = workers x 2n bound vectors; queue = heap records + per-node payload. Baseline queue payload counts per-node full bound vectors, basis copy and deep cut copy; current queue payload counts sizeof(BranchNode) + delta-chain bytes with the shared basis and shared NodeCuts payload counted once. Allocator metadata and strings excluded (strings empty/SSO in these runs).
structural_accounting.parameters: MODE NODES 1024 1024 4 32 4 [FILL]: 1024 variables, basis 1024, 4 cuts x 32 coefficients, 4 workers; FILL extra nonzeros per column (diagonal + FILL-1 fill entries).
structural_accounting.reading: Queue bytes scale linearly with node count and are identical across a 61x root-matrix growth (root_bytes 69640 -> 4247560), while root and worker classes are constant across the node sweep. The materialized baseline queue grows to 169.5 MB at 4000 nodes versus 0.84 MB for the persistent representation (~201x at equal content).

full_solver_frontier.measure: Result::max_queued_nodes (new peak-frontier field), queue_records_bytes = max_queued_nodes * sizeof(BranchNode) (lower bound: delta chains, shared cut payloads and LP workspaces excluded), root_bytes, getrusage ru_maxrss, plus a 10 ms resident sampler and 250 ms signal-tick high-water for spike localization.
full_solver_frontier.reading: Real solves show frontier growth (flugpl peak queue 47 -> 531 nodes across caps) with queue record bytes in the tens of kilobytes and peak RSS tracking root/LP workspace size, not queue growth; frontier and RSS evidence no longer rests on the synthetic bench alone.

acceptance_mapping.sibling_branch_mutation_isolation: reference_materialisation_test::test_sibling_isolation (bounds, cuts and parent immutability after branching) plus existing node_view_test sibling coverage.
acceptance_mapping.randomized_push_pop_matches_full_reconst: test_randomized_chains (200 trials) and test_push_pop_reversibility (400 random push/pop ops compared against chronological replay of the retained prefix).
acceptance_mapping.identical_original_space_solutions_certi: Element-wise bound-vector equality between production and reference feeds identical node LP inputs; node_view_reference_identity_test requires bit-identical node-LP status/objective/primal from both paths and verify_primal passes against the original model for node and full-solve certificates; full suite 89/89 in Release, ASan/UBSan and TSan.
acceptance_mapping.allocation_measurements_distinguish_root: Structural accounting reports root_bytes, worker_bytes and queue_bytes separately in both bench modes; constants verified across the node sweep.
acceptance_mapping.queue_growth_does_not_multiply_full_matr: Fill sweep: root_bytes grows 61x while queue_bytes are byte-identical in both modes; node sweep: queue_bytes linear in nodes while root/worker classes stay flat; full-solver queue_records_bytes stay <= 121 KB while frontier grows to 1001 nodes.
acceptance_mapping.baseline_retained_only_as_bounded_regres: The materialized baseline remains in bench_node_frontier_memory for measurement only, and the comparator oracle refuses over-cap requests before allocating (asserted reference_bytes=0); no production path materializes per-node full copies.

observation_transient_rss_spike.what: Five runs recorded peak_rss_kib exactly 1013492 (~990 MiB) as a transient: pk1 (2x, plain runs), sp150x300d (2x, plain runs), gen-ip002 (1x, instrumented).
observation_transient_rss_spike.localization: In the instrumented gen-ip002 occurrence the 250 ms signal tick saw the high-water at tick 0 while the 10 ms resident sampler never exceeded 6844 KiB, so the event is a short-lived ~1 GiB footprint during the first 250 ms (parse/root phase), not steady-state growth. Normal runs of the same commands peak at 5-20 MiB.
observation_transient_rss_spike.queue_excluded: Queue records in occurrence runs were <= 82680 bytes; the spike is not queue storage.
observation_transient_rss_spike.reproduction_attempts: Not reproduced by 7 runs under an LD_PRELOAD malloc/calloc/realloc interposer (16 MiB logging threshold, zero large allocations logged), 8 further clean gen-ip002 runs, or 13 instrumented sp150x300d runs; overall roughly 5 of ~35 eligible runs. Occurred only in time-limited runs in the observed sample, but one instrumented occurrence was within the first 250 ms (before any deadline), so a deadline-only explanation does not hold.
observation_transient_rss_spike.status: Root cause not investigated under IR-19 scope. Recorded here as a candidate for dedicated follow-up; directly relevant to IR-21 (solve-wide memory budget, backlog item 5) because a budgeted cap would bound it even before the root cause is found.

limitations: Structural bench nodes each carry a one-delta chain rooted at an empty parent (exact accounting by construction); in real searches chains are shared with ancestors and retained_bytes is a per-node full-chain figure, so summing it over a tree over-counts shared links (upper bound).
Full-solver queue_records_bytes counts heap records only: delta-chain payloads, shared cut/basis payloads and all LP/QP workspaces are outside it, so it is a lower bound on queue storage.

Worker-class storage remains by design: the serial mutable node-model workspace, per-worker bound overlays and the sparse-PDLP fallback materialization are measured as worker_bytes in the synthetic bench but not itemized inside a live solve.
The transient ~1 GiB RSS anomaly above is unexplained; full-solver RSS numbers exclude the five occurrence runs from the tables.
All measurements are single-host, single-process, Linux glibc; allocator metadata and strings are excluded from byte accounting.
This evidence closes IR-19 against the W01 acceptance list only; IR-20/21 and the engine-consumption gaps of items 2/3 remain open.
conclusion: All six W01 acceptance criteria are demonstrated: bounded reference replay agrees with production on randomized and push/pop chains while refusing over-cap requests before allocating; sibling isolation and original-space certificate identity are test-gated; root, worker and queue storage are measured as distinct classes; and queue growth is shown independent of matrix fill in both synthetic and full-solver runs, with the materialized baseline retained only as a measurement oracle. IR-19 is closed on this evidence with the remaining worker-class storage and the transient RSS anomaly explicitly scoped out and handed to item 5 / IR-21 follow-up.
